ev.mng_h_dalan.title: Temüjin or Jamukha
ev.mng_h_dalan.text: The former anda Temüjin and Jamukha have parted, and the steppe has split in two. They say that after his victory at Dalan Baljut Jamukha boiled captive youths in seventy cauldrons - and many of his own men have gone over to Temüjin, who shares the spoils fairly.
ev.mng_h_dalan.temujin.ok: You bring your yurt into Temüjin's camp. Here a nöker is valued above noble birth.
ev.mng_h_dalan.jamukha.ok: You stay with Jamukha. The old clans are on his side - but luck, it seems, is not.
ev.mng_h_dalan.note: Temüjin and Jamukha swore anda three times, but around 1187 they became enemies. Jamukha won at Dalan Baljut, yet his cruelty drove away his allies. According to the Secret History, many clans went over to Temüjin.
ev.mng_h_tatars.title: The campaign against the Tatars
ev.mng_h_tatars.text: Together with the Kereit Wang Khan and the Jin armies, Temüjin is marching on the Tatars - the men who poisoned his father. Every clan sends riders.
ev.mng_h_tatars.go.success: The Tatars are broken. Your share is a horse and a silver bowl from the Tatar camp.
ev.mng_h_tatars.go.failure: A Tatar arrow strikes your thigh. You come home before everyone else.
ev.mng_h_tatars.stay.ok: You stay behind with the livestock. The spoils are shared without you.
ev.mng_h_tatars.note: In 1196 Temüjin and the Kereit Wang Khan helped the Jin empire crush the Tatars. The Jin granted Temüjin a title, which strengthened his position on the steppe.
ev.mng_h_baljuna.title: The muddy water of Baljuna
ev.mng_h_baljuna.text: Wang Khan has betrayed Temüjin, who is defeated. Only a few remain with him at Lake Baljuna. Temüjin scoops up muddy water and swears: "If I achieve my aim, I will share with you the sweet and the bitter." The cup goes round.
ev.mng_h_baljuna.drink.ok: You drink. From now on you are one of "those who drank the water of Baljuna" - Chinggis will never forget them.
ev.mng_h_baljuna.leave.ok: You go over to the stronger side. It is sensible. Why, then, is it so shameful?
ev.mng_h_baljuna.note: In the summer of 1203, after his defeat by the Kereits, Temüjin fell back to Baljuna with a small band. By tradition his companions swore loyalty by drinking its muddy water. Later the "Baljuntu" were richly rewarded.
ev.mng_h_baljuna_reward.title: The reward for Baljuna
ev.mng_h_baljuna_reward.text: Chinggis has not forgotten: to everyone who drank the water of Baljuna he grants pastures, people, and the right to enter his presence unsummoned.
ev.mng_h_naimans.title: The Uyghur script
ev.mng_h_naimans.text: After the Naimans were crushed, their keeper of the seal, the Uyghur Tatatunga, was taken prisoner. Chinggis has ordered him to teach the sons of the nobles to write in Uyghur - now the Mongols will have letters of their own.
ev.mng_h_naimans.note: According to the Yuan Shi, in 1204, after the victory over the Naimans, Chinggis Khan had the captive Uyghur Tatatunga teach writing to his sons. So the Uyghur script became the Mongol script and has survived to this day.
ev.mng_h_kurultai1206.title: The Great Kurultai
ev.mng_h_kurultai1206.text: At the source of the Onon the white nine-tailed standard has been raised. All the clans of the steppe have gathered at the kurultai and named Temüjin Chinggis Khan. From now on there are no Naimans, no Tatars, no Tayichi'ud - only one people of the felt walls, divided into tens, hundreds and thousands.
ev.mng_h_kurultai1206.swear.ok: You are entered in a thousand. Your leader of ten is a stranger from another clan - and that no longer matters.
ev.mng_h_kurultai1206.grumble.ok: You swear like everyone else, but privately count how many old chiefs did not live to see this day.
ev.mng_h_kurultai1206.note: In 1206, at a kurultai at the source of the Onon, Temüjin was proclaimed Chinggis Khan. He divided the people into 95 thousands headed by his nökers, founded the keshig guard and, by tradition, proclaimed the yasa.
ev.mng_h_xixia.title: The campaign against the Tanguts
ev.mng_h_xixia.text: The khan leads the army against the Tangut kingdom of Xi Xia. Under the walls of its capital the Mongols are learning for the first time how to take cities: they build a dam to flood it - and nearly drown themselves.
ev.mng_h_xixia.go.success: The Tangut king hands over his daughter and camels. You come back with spoils.
ev.mng_h_xixia.go.failure: The water bursts the dam and sweeps away the camp. You barely get out alive.
ev.mng_h_xixia.stay.ok: You tend the herds while others make war.
ev.mng_h_xixia.note: In 1209-1210 Chinggis Khan besieged the capital of the Tangut state of Xi Xia. The Mongols tried to flood the city by diverting the river, but the dam burst and flooded their own camp. The Tangut ruler nevertheless submitted as a tributary.
ev.mng_h_jin.title: The Great Wall
ev.mng_h_jin.text: The Mongols have gone south beyond the Great Wall against the Jin empire. Cities fall one after another, and in 1215 the capital Zhongdu itself falls. Every ten comes back with silk, silver and captive craftsmen.
ev.mng_h_jin.go.success: You return with a bale of silk and a captive craftsman who can make porcelain.
ev.mng_h_jin.go.failure: A Chinese crossbow bolt pierces your armour. You are carried home in a wagon.
ev.mng_h_jin.stay.ok: You are left out: your ten rides off without you.
ev.mng_h_jin.note: In 1211 Chinggis Khan began his war with the Jurchen Jin empire. In 1215 the Mongols took and sacked its capital Zhongdu (the future Beijing). The war with the Jin ended only under Ögedei in 1234.
ev.mng_h_otrar.title: The war with Khwarazm
ev.mng_h_otrar.text: At Otrar the Khwarazmian governor massacred the khan's caravan and his envoys. The khan has roused the whole steppe: two hundred thousand riders are heading west - against Otrar, Bukhara, Samarkand, Urgench.
ev.mng_h_otrar.go.success: You return from Transoxiana with silver and captive weavers. But for a long time burning cities stay before your eyes.
ev.mng_h_otrar.go.failure: Under the walls of Urgench you are struck by a sling stone. There is no booty, and the wound aches before bad weather.
ev.mng_h_otrar.stay.ok: You stay to guard the camps. Three years later not everyone comes back.
ev.mng_h_otrar.note: In 1218 Inalchuq, governor of Otrar, massacred a Mongol trade caravan, and the Khwarazmshah Muhammad executed an envoy. In 1219-1221 Chinggis Khan destroyed the Khwarazmian state: Otrar, Bukhara, Samarkand, Urgench and Merv fell.
ev.mng_h_kalka.title: The battle on the Kalka
ev.mng_h_kalka.text: The tümens of Jebe and Sübe'etei have come back from their ride round the Caspian. They tell of a battle with an unknown people - the Urus - on the river Kalka: the princes came separately and died separately.
ev.mng_h_kalka.note: In 1223 on the river Kalka the force of Jebe and Sübe'etei defeated the armies of the Russian princes and the Cumans. It was the first clash between Rus and the Mongols; the Mongols then withdrew and returned only thirteen years later.
ev.mng_h_chinggis_death.title: The death of Chinggis Khan
ev.mng_h_chinggis_death.text: Heralds bring terrible news: Chinggis Khan has died on campaign against the Tanguts. His body is being carried home to the Burkhan Khaldun mountains, and they say that anyone met on the road is killed, so that no one will know where the grave lies.
ev.mng_h_chinggis_death.note: Chinggis Khan died in August 1227 during the campaign against Xi Xia. He was buried in secret, probably in the Khentii mountains. The tales of everyone met on the road being killed, and of herds trampling the grave, are legends recorded later.
ev.mng_h_karakorum_built.title: The walls of Karakorum
ev.mng_h_karakorum_built.text: Khan Ögedei has ordered a wall built round the camp on the Orkhon. People are rounded up from all over the steppe to haul clay and stone, while captive Chinese craftsmen build the palace of Tümen Amgalan - "Ten Thousand Peaces".
ev.mng_h_karakorum_built.work.ok: All summer you haul clay with your oxen. The silver from the khan's treasury is real.
ev.mng_h_karakorum_built.avoid.ok: You take your yurt off to the far hills. Let them build without you.
ev.mng_h_karakorum_built.note: Karakorum became the capital of the Mongol Empire under Ögedei: in 1235 the city was walled and a palace built there. Excavations confirm quarters of craftsmen and merchants.
ev.mng_h_yam.title: The relay stations
ev.mng_h_yam.text: Ögedei has ordered yams - relay stations - set up across the whole empire, one every thirty or forty versts. Every thousand supplies horses, men and sheep. A man is needed for the yam from your camp too.
ev.mng_h_yam.serve.ok: Now you are a yam courier: day and night you keep fresh horses for the khan's messengers.
ev.mng_h_yam.pay.ok: You give three horses to the yam. Let others serve.
ev.mng_h_yam.note: The yam relay system was organised under Ögedei around 1234. Stations stood 30-50 km apart, and couriers bearing a paiza received fresh horses and covered up to 200-300 km a day.
ev.mng_h_batu_west.title: Batu's campaign
ev.mng_h_batu_west.text: The kurultai has decided: the eldest sons of every clan are to ride west with Batu - against the Kipchaks, the Bulgars and the Urus. In winter, over the frozen rivers, the tümens reach the forest cities: Ryazan, Vladimir, Kozelsk, which the khan called the "wicked city".
ev.mng_h_batu_west.go.success: You return with sables, silver grivnas and stories of wooden cities in the endless forest.
ev.mng_h_batu_west.go.failure: At Kozelsk you are wounded so badly you cannot sit a saddle for a long time.
ev.mng_h_batu_west.stay.ok: You are kept back with the herds - someone has to tend them.
ev.mng_h_batu_west.note: In 1236-1242 the army of Batu and Sübe'etei conquered Volga Bulgaria, the Cumans and the Russian principalities. Ryazan (1237), Vladimir (1238) and Kiev (1240) were devastated; Kozelsk held out for seven weeks.
ev.mng_h_legnica.title: The land of the Franks
ev.mng_h_legnica.text: The tümens have crossed Poland and Hungary: at Legnica and on the river Sajó the knights in iron have been beaten. Ahead, they say, lie the sea and the land of the Franks. But then a messenger gallops in from the steppe: Khan Ögedei is dead, and the princes are turning their horses for the kurultai.
ev.mng_h_legnica.note: In April 1241 the Mongols defeated the Poles and Germans at Legnica and the Hungarians on the Sajó (Mohi), and reached the Adriatic. In December 1241 Ögedei died, and in 1242 the army turned back.
ev.mng_h_mongke_purge.title: Möngke's kurultai
ev.mng_h_mongke_purge.text: The descendants of Tolui and Jochi have put Möngke on the throne. Ögedei's grandsons refused to recognise him and, they say, came to the kurultai with weapons hidden in their wagons. Now their supporters are being hunted through every ulus.
ev.mng_h_mongke_purge.bow.ok: You kneel and give nine white horses. You are left alone.
ev.mng_h_mongke_purge.hide: Hide a friend of Ögedei's line
ev.mng_h_mongke_purge.hide.success: Your friend gets away to Khaidu in the Seven Rivers. No one finds out.
ev.mng_h_mongke_purge.hide.failure: He is found in your wagon. Only the khan's mercy saves you - that, and half your herd.
ev.mng_h_mongke_purge.note: In 1251 Möngke, son of Tolui, was elected Great Khan at a kurultai. Uncovering a plot by the descendants of Ögedei and Chagatai, he executed many of their supporters; it was the first deep rift within the Chinggisid line.
ev.mng_h_census.title: Möngke's census
ev.mng_h_census.text: People and livestock are being registered across the whole empire: one head in every hundred for the treasury, and the qubchur tax from every adult. Scribes go from yurt to yurt with their books, counting the sheep.
ev.mng_h_census.honest.ok: The scribe writes everything down. The tax is heavy, but you sleep easy.
ev.mng_h_census.hide: Hide part of it in a gully
ev.mng_h_census.hide.success: Half the herd grazes in a gully while the scribes count the rest.
ev.mng_h_census.hide.failure: A neighbour shows the scribes the gully. The tax is taken twice over.
ev.mng_h_census.note: Under Möngke in the 1250s a census of people and livestock was carried out across the empire. A tax on livestock (qubchur) and a poll tax were introduced; in 1257-1259 the census was also carried out in Rus.
ev.mng_h_baghdad.title: Baghdad
ev.mng_h_baghdad.text: Hülegü's army has taken Baghdad - the city of the caliphs, richer than any under the Sky. For a week it is plundered. The waters of the Tigris run black with ink: books from the libraries are being thrown into the river. You are standing at the shattered gates of the House of Wisdom.
ev.mng_h_baghdad.loot.ok: You stuff your saddlebags with gold dishes and silk. Behind you the city burns.
ev.mng_h_baghdad.books.ok: You carry an armful of books out of the fire and give them to the astronomer Nasir al-Din Tusi, who serves Hülegü. He looks at you for a long time without a word.
ev.mng_h_baghdad.note: In February 1258 Hülegü's troops took Baghdad after a two-week siege. The last Abbasid caliph, al-Musta'sim, was executed, the city sacked, and tens of thousands of its people killed. The astronomer Nasir al-Din Tusi carried some of the books off to the observatory at Maragha.
ev.mng_h_ain_jalut.title: Ain Jalut
ev.mng_h_ain_jalut.text: Kitbuqa's tümen, left behind in Syria, has been routed by the Egyptian Mamluks at Ain Jalut - "Goliath's Spring". Kitbuqa himself is dead. For the first time the Mongols have been stopped.
ev.mng_h_ain_jalut.note: On 3 September 1260 the Mamluks of Sultan Qutuz and Baybars defeated Kitbuqa's Mongol force at Ain Jalut in Palestine. It halted the Mongol advance on Egypt.
ev.mng_h_civil_war.title: Two khans
ev.mng_h_civil_war.text: Two brothers, Khubilai and Ariq Böke, have each proclaimed himself Great Khan. Khubilai has cut off the grain supply from China, and there is hunger in Karakorum. The noyans are choosing sides.
ev.mng_h_civil_war.ariq: For Ariq Böke and the steppe
ev.mng_h_civil_war.ariq.ok: You stand by the steppe khan. But there is less and less bread in Karakorum.
ev.mng_h_civil_war.khubilai.ok: You move over to Khubilai. His army is well fed, and there is Chinese rice in his baggage train.
ev.mng_h_civil_war.note: After Möngke's death in 1259, his brothers Khubilai and Ariq Böke were proclaimed khan at rival kurultais in 1260. Khubilai cut Karakorum off from its supplies from China, and in 1264 Ariq Böke surrendered.
ev.mng_h_berke.title: Mongol against Mongol
ev.mng_h_berke.text: Berke, khan of the Ulus of Jochi and a Muslim convert, has gone to war against Hülegü over the sack of Baghdad and the disputed pastures of Azerbaijan. On the ice of the Terek, Mongols fight Mongols.
ev.mng_h_berke.go.success: The ice held under you and broke beneath them. You come back alive.
ev.mng_h_berke.go.failure: You are wounded in the first clash. Berke, they say, wept: "Mongols are killing Mongols."
ev.mng_h_berke.stay.ok: You do not go to spill your own people's blood.
ev.mng_h_berke.note: In 1262 war broke out between Berke, khan of the Golden Horde, and the Ilkhan Hülegü - the first open war between the uluses of the empire. In 1263 Hülegü's army was defeated on the Terek, and some of his men fell through the ice.
ev.mng_h_yuan.title: The Great Yuan
ev.mng_h_yuan.text: Khubilai has proclaimed a new name for his realm in the Chinese manner - Da Yuan, the "Great Origin". Heralds read the decree in the squares of Khanbaliq: from now on the khan is also the Son of Heaven.
ev.mng_h_yuan.note: In 1271 Khubilai proclaimed the Yuan dynasty, and in 1272 made Dadu (Khanbaliq), on the site of present-day Beijing, his capital. The Mongols became the ruling people over all of China.
ev.mng_h_xiangyang.title: The siege of Xiangyang
ev.mng_h_xiangyang.text: For five years the Mongols have stood before Xiangyang, the key to southern China. Muslim engineers from Iran have built trebuchets that hurl boulders half a verst. Men are needed for the machines.
ev.mng_h_xiangyang.go.success: A boulder from your trebuchet smashes a tower. The city surrenders within a week.
ev.mng_h_xiangyang.go.failure: A slipping arm strikes you on the shoulder.
ev.mng_h_xiangyang.note: The siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng lasted from 1268 to 1273. It was decided by counterweight trebuchets built by the engineers Ismail and Ala al-Din, sent by the Ilkhan. After that the Southern Song fell by 1279.
ev.mng_h_japan.title: The fleet against Japan
ev.mng_h_japan.text: Khubilai has assembled a vast fleet - thousands of ships from Korea and southern China - to conquer the island of Japan. Everyone who can sit a horse and does not fear the water is being enlisted.
ev.mng_h_japan.go.success: A typhoon scatters the fleet off Kyushu. By a miracle your ship limps back to Korea.
ev.mng_h_japan.go.failure: The wind of the gods, as the Japanese call it, smashes the ships. You are thrown onto a foreign shore.
ev.mng_h_japan.stay.ok: You buy your way out of the levy. A month later word comes that the fleet is lost.
ev.mng_h_japan.note: In the summer of 1281 the Yuan fleet (about 4,000 ships) tried to land on Kyushu but was destroyed by a typhoon - called kamikaze, the "divine wind", in Japan. It was the second failed attempt after 1274.
ev.mng_h_marco.title: A Latin at court
ev.mng_h_marco.text: A young Latin from Venice named Marco serves at the khan's court. The khan sends him round the provinces and loves to hear his tales of distant lands. He questions you about steppe customs and writes everything down.
ev.mng_h_marco.note: The Venetian Marco Polo, by his own account, spent some seventeen years at Khubilai's court (1275-1292). His Description of the World became the Europeans' main source on China; historians dispute some of its details.
ev.mng_h_ghazan.title: Ilkhan Mahmud Ghazan
ev.mng_h_ghazan.text: The Ilkhan Ghazan has embraced Islam and taken the name Mahmud, and tens of thousands of Mongol soldiers have followed him. The Buddhist temples of Tabriz are being closed, and Mongol noyans are putting on turbans.
ev.mng_h_ghazan.convert: Become a Muslim with the khan
ev.mng_h_ghazan.convert.ok: You recite the shahada in the mosque together with your hundred.
ev.mng_h_ghazan.keep.ok: You pray in the old way - quietly, in your own yurt.
ev.mng_h_ghazan.note: In 1295 the Ilkhan Ghazan converted to Islam. Many Mongols of his army followed him; Buddhist temples in Iran were destroyed. Under Ghazan the vizier Rashid al-Din reformed taxation and began his Compendium of Chronicles.
ev.mng_h_rashid.title: The execution of Rashid al-Din
ev.mng_h_rashid.text: The grand vizier Rashid al-Din - physician and historian, who wrote a history of all the peoples of the world - has been accused of poisoning the Ilkhan and executed. His quarter, the Rab-i Rashidi, with its library and hospital, has been plundered.
ev.mng_h_rashid.note: Rashid al-Din Fazlullah Hamadani, vizier of the Ilkhans and author of the Jami al-Tawarikh, was executed in 1318 on a charge of poisoning the Ilkhan Öljeitü. The Rab-i Rashidi quarter he had founded in Tabriz was plundered.
ev.mng_h_ilkhan_end.title: The end of the Ilkhans
ev.mng_h_ilkhan_end.text: The Ilkhan Abu Sa'id has died without a son, and the realm has crumbled: emirs put puppets on the throne and cut each other down. Mongols in Iran feel ill at ease - many are moving away.
ev.mng_h_ilkhan_end.stay.ok: You stay. Persian is now heard in your yurt more often than Mongol.
ev.mng_h_ilkhan_end.east.ok: You leave with a caravan for the Onon, the land of your ancestors.
ev.mng_h_ilkhan_end.note: After the Ilkhan Abu Sa'id died in 1335 without an heir, the Hülegüid state broke up into the domains of rival emirs - the Jalayirids, the Chobanids and others.
ev.mng_h_uzbek.title: Khan Özbeg
ev.mng_h_uzbek.text: The new khan, Özbeg, has proclaimed Islam the faith of the Horde. Princes and shamans who objected, they say, have been killed. A great mosque and madrasa are going up in Sarai - and yet Russian priests are still granted patents.
ev.mng_h_uzbek.note: Khan Özbeg (1313-1341) made Islam the state religion of the Golden Horde. Under him the Horde was at its height: Sarai became one of the largest cities in the world, and Ibn Battuta visited it.
ev.mng_h_tver.title: Tver
ev.mng_h_tver.text: The townsfolk of Tver have risen and burned the khan's envoy Chol Khan alive with his men. The khan is sending five commanders of tümens - and with them Prince Ivan of Moscow, who is seeking the patent of grand prince.
ev.mng_h_tver.go.success: Tver is laid waste, and you come back with captives and furs.
ev.mng_h_tver.go.failure: In the forests of Tver your hundred is cut down from ambush.
ev.mng_h_tver.stay.ok: Let the Urus cut each other down themselves.
ev.mng_h_tver.note: In August 1327 an uprising broke out in Tver against the Horde envoy Chol Khan (Shchelkan), who was killed with his retinue. Khan Özbeg sent a punitive army in which Prince Ivan Kalita of Moscow rode; afterwards Moscow received the patent for the grand principality.
ev.mng_h_great_trouble.title: The Great Troubles
ev.mng_h_great_trouble.text: In twenty years more than twenty khans have come and gone in Sarai: each one cuts down his predecessor and his children. The commander Mamai, though no Chinggisid, rules the west of the Horde in the name of his puppets.
ev.mng_h_great_trouble.note: After the murder of Khan Berdibek in 1359 the Golden Horde entered the "Great Troubles" - twenty years of turmoil in which some twenty-five khans came and went. The western part of the Horde was effectively ruled by the commander Mamai.
ev.mng_h_kulikovo.title: The field of Kulikovo
ev.mng_h_kulikovo.text: Mamai is leading an army into Rus to punish Prince Dmitry of Moscow, who has stopped paying the tribute. With him march Genoese infantry from Caffa and mercenaries. The muster is at the Don.
ev.mng_h_kulikovo.go.success: The slaughter is terrible. You survive and get away into the steppe when the ambush regiment strikes from the oak wood.
ev.mng_h_kulikovo.go.failure: The Russian ambush regiment crushes your flank. You come to among the bodies on the bank of the Nepryadva.
ev.mng_h_kulikovo.stay.ok: You do not follow the upstart Mamai. Nor do many others.
ev.mng_h_kulikovo.note: On 8 September 1380, on the field of Kulikovo by the Don, Prince Dmitry Ivanovich of Moscow (Donskoy) defeated Mamai's army. Two years later Khan Tokhtamysh burned Moscow and restored the tribute, but the victory became a symbol of Russia's liberation.
ev.mng_h_tokhtamysh.title: Moscow burns
ev.mng_h_tokhtamysh.text: Khan Tokhtamysh, who has overthrown Mamai, is suddenly marching on Moscow. Prince Dmitry has left to gather an army, and the townsfolk held the walls for three days - until they were promised peace.
ev.mng_h_tokhtamysh.go.ok: The gates open, and the army bursts in. You come back with silver - and with the smell of burning, which will not air out.
ev.mng_h_tokhtamysh.guard.ok: You guard the herds while Moscow burns.
ev.mng_h_tokhtamysh.note: In August 1382 Khan Tokhtamysh took Moscow by deceit after a three-day siege and burned it. Payment of tribute to the Horde was restored.
ev.mng_h_timur.title: The Iron Lame One
ev.mng_h_timur.text: Timur, lord of Samarkand, has crushed Tokhtamysh on the Terek and is advancing along the Volga. Sarai is burning, and its craftsmen are being driven off to Samarkand. Of the great city there remain only charred beams and empty mosques.
ev.mng_h_timur.flee.ok: You escape into the steppe with a single wagon. There will be nothing to come back to.
ev.mng_h_timur.hide.success: You sit in a cellar for three days. The city burns down, but you live.
ev.mng_h_timur.hide.failure: You are found and driven off with the craftsmen to Samarkand.
ev.mng_h_timur.note: In 1395 Timur defeated Khan Tokhtamysh on the Terek and then laid waste the cities of the Golden Horde, including Sarai-Berke and Hajji Tarkhan. The Horde never recovered from the blow.
ev.mng_h_ugra.title: The stand on the Ugra
ev.mng_h_ugra.text: Khan Akhmat has brought the Great Horde to the river Ugra: Ivan of Moscow has stopped paying. For a month the armies stand on opposite banks, exchanging arrows across the river. The frosts have come, and the Lithuanians who were promised have not.
ev.mng_h_ugra.note: In the autumn of 1480 the armies of Akhmat, khan of the Great Horde, and Grand Prince Ivan III faced each other for several weeks on the river Ugra. Akhmat withdrew without daring to give battle; this is regarded as the end of the Horde's yoke over Rus.
ev.mng_h_sarai_end.title: The end of the Horde
ev.mng_h_sarai_end.text: The Crimean khan Mengli Giray has crushed the last khan of the Great Horde and burned Sarai. The uluses have scattered - some to Kazan, some to Astrakhan, some to the Nogais.
ev.mng_h_sarai_end.note: In 1502 the Crimean khan Mengli I Giray defeated the army of Sheikh Ahmed, khan of the Great Horde, and laid waste its capital. The Great Horde - the last remnant of the Golden Horde - ceased to exist.
ev.mng_h_red_turbans.title: The Red Turbans
ev.mng_h_red_turbans.text: A hundred and fifty thousand men were rounded up to repair the Yellow River dykes, and there a revolt has broken out. Rebels in red headbands say the Buddha of the future is coming and that the Mongol Heaven is finished. The south no longer pays its taxes.
ev.mng_h_red_turbans.note: In 1351 the Red Turban rebellion, linked to the White Lotus sect, broke out among the labourers conscripted to repair the Yellow River dykes. It engulfed all of China; from among its leaders came Zhu Yuanzhang, founder of the Ming dynasty.
ev.mng_h_flight1368.title: Flight from Khanbaliq
ev.mng_h_flight1368.text: The Ming armies are at the gates. Khan Toghon Temür slips out of the capital by night through the northern gate - to Shangdu, to the steppe his forefathers came from. Behind him trail the wagons of nobles, scribes and servants.
ev.mng_h_flight1368.flee: Go with the khan to the steppe
ev.mng_h_flight1368.flee.ok: You look back at the walls of Khanbaliq one last time. Ahead lies the steppe you knew only from songs.
ev.mng_h_flight1368.stay.ok: You trade your deel for a Chinese robe and learn a new name. The Ming do not love Mongols, but they do not touch them all.
ev.mng_h_flight1368.note: In September 1368, as the Ming armies approached Dadu, the last Yuan emperor Toghon Temür fled to Shangdu and then to Mongolia. The Mongol khans continued to rule on the steppe - their realm is called the Northern Yuan.
ev.mng_h_karakorum_burned.title: Ming troops on the steppe
ev.mng_h_karakorum_burned.text: The Chinese armies of the Ming have come into the steppe itself: Karakorum has been burned, and at Lake Buir tens of thousands of Mongols and the khan's family have been taken prisoner. The old men say nothing like this has happened since before Chinggis.
ev.mng_h_karakorum_burned.note: In 1380 Ming troops burned Karakorum, and in 1388 General Lan Yu routed Khan Tögüs Temür at Lake Buir, taking some 70,000 prisoners. Soon afterwards the khan was murdered, and the Northern Yuan broke up into warring parts.
ev.mng_h_tumu.title: An emperor captured
ev.mng_h_tumu.text: The Oirat ruler Esen has routed a huge Ming army at Tumu and taken the Chinese emperor himself prisoner. The captive is carried about the steppe while Esen ponders what to do with him.
ev.mng_h_tumu.note: In September 1449 the Oirat Esen Taishi defeated the Ming army at the fortress of Tumu and captured the Zhengtong emperor. The emperor was released a year later; in 1453 Esen proclaimed himself khan but was soon killed.
ev.mng_h_mandukhai.title: Mandukhai the Wise
ev.mng_h_mandukhai.text: The khan's widow Mandukhai has married the boy Batmönkh - the last of Chinggis's line - and is herself leading the army against the Oirats, with a cradle tied to her saddle. They say she fought while with child.
ev.mng_h_mandukhai.join.success: The Oirats are broken. Mandukhai herself offers you a bowl of kumis.
ev.mng_h_mandukhai.join.failure: You are wounded in a skirmish at the pass, but the victory is hers.
ev.mng_h_mandukhai.stay.ok: You tend the livestock while the camps sing of the warrior queen.
ev.mng_h_mandukhai.note: Mandukhai Khatun (c. 1449-1510), after her husband's death, married the young Batmönkh, the future Dayan Khan, and led the armies against the Oirats. Tradition calls her the saviour of the Chinggisid line.
ev.mng_h_dayan.title: The six tümens
ev.mng_h_dayan.text: Dayan Khan has defeated the rebel western tümens at Dalan Terigün and once more gathered the eastern Mongols under one hand. From now on the steppe is divided into six tümens, and his sons will become khans of each.
ev.mng_h_dayan.note: Dayan Khan (Batmönkh, c. 1464-1517/1543) defeated the right-wing tümens at Dalan Terigün around 1510 and united the eastern Mongols. He divided them into six tümens and set his own descendants at their head.
ev.mng_h_altan_beijing.title: Beneath the walls of Beijing
ev.mng_h_altan_beijing.text: Altan Khan demands that the Ming open horse markets, and when refused he leads his tümens to Beijing itself. The countryside burns, and the emperor is afraid. Your hundred is riding on the raid.
ev.mng_h_altan_beijing.go.success: You come back with silk, tea and iron pots.
ev.mng_h_altan_beijing.go.failure: A Chinese cannon strikes your hundred. You barely get out.
ev.mng_h_altan_beijing.note: In 1550 Altan Khan of the Tümed, seeking the opening of border trade, besieged the outskirts of Beijing. Peace was made in 1571: the Ming opened horse markets and gave Altan the title "Prince Shunyi".
ev.mng_h_dalai.title: The Dalai Lama
ev.mng_h_dalai.text: By Lake Kokonor Altan Khan has met the Tibetan lama Sonam Gyatso and named him Dalai Lama - "Ocean of Wisdom". In return the lama has declared the khan a rebirth of Khubilai. Couriers are carrying the news to every camp.
ev.mng_h_dalai.note: In 1578 the Tümed ruler Altan Khan met Sonam Gyatso, head of the Gelug school, and gave him the title of Dalai Lama. This began the mass conversion of the Mongols to Tibetan Buddhism.
ev.mng_h_erdene_zuu.title: Erdene Zuu
ev.mng_h_erdene_zuu.text: Abtai Khan is building the monastery of Erdene Zuu right on the ruins of Karakorum - out of its very stones. A hundred and eight stupas will rise round its walls, and pilgrims are already arriving with gifts.
ev.mng_h_erdene_zuu.give.ok: You drive five sheep to the monastery. A lama ties a khadag scarf round your neck.
ev.mng_h_erdene_zuu.look.ok: You wander among the old turtles and new stupas and think that the Sky is fond of change.
ev.mng_h_erdene_zuu.note: The monastery of Erdene Zuu was founded by Abtai Khan of the Khalkha in 1585 on the site of ancient Karakorum, using stones from the ruins of the capital. It was the first great Buddhist monastery of Mongolia.
ev.mng_h_ibn_battuta.title: A traveller from the Maghreb
ev.mng_h_ibn_battuta.text: A scholar-judge from distant Tangier has come to Sarai - Ibn Battuta. He marvels at the breadth of the streets and at how the Mongol khatuns drive their own wagons and receive guests with their faces uncovered.
ev.mng_h_ibn_battuta.note: Ibn Battuta visited the Golden Horde around 1333-1334 and described Sarai as a huge city with fine bazaars. He was especially struck by the high standing of women among the Turks and Mongols.
ev.mng_h_rubruck.title: The Frankish friar
ev.mng_h_rubruck.text: A barefoot friar from the land of the Franks - William - has arrived at the khan's court. He is looking for Christians, hands out incense and is forever writing things down. The khan's people laugh that he cannot drink kumis.
ev.mng_h_rubruck.note: The Franciscan William of Rubruck, on behalf of King Louis IX of France, visited Khan Möngke at Karakorum in 1253-1255. His detailed report is one of the best sources on life in the Mongol capital.
ev.mng_h_plague_yuan.title: Pestilence and famine
ev.mng_h_plague_yuan.text: Drought, locusts, the floods of the Yellow River - and after them pestilence. In the provinces whole districts are dying out. Crowds of the hungry are streaming into the capital, and the price of rice rises every day.
ev.mng_h_plague_yuan.note: In the early 1330s Yuan China suffered severe droughts, floods and famine; in 1331 the chronicles report a great epidemic in Henan province. Some historians link it to the beginning of the Black Death, but this is disputed.
